Meta Platforms Inc (META.O) Meta’s AI Product Roadmap Emerging as Compute Scales with Multiple Paths for Monetization CITI'S TAKE While 2Q revenues & 3Q guidance were largely in-line with expectations, we emerge from the quarter incrementally positive on Meta’s product strategy, while acknowledging the debates around continued CapEx spend, tangible ROI, and profitability. Most importantly, we believe Meta’s LLMs are beginning to deliver durable engagement gains on continued R&R improvements and we note global time spent on IG rose DD in 2Q. And with 1M+ businesses using Business Agent, 9M+ SMBs using Meta’s AI creative tools, as newer apps launch and Meta’s subscription offering ramps, we believe there is increasing clarity on Meta’s product roadmap, and we await details of Meta’s Enterprise offering. While we expect Meta to continue investing in its infrastructure, we also believe newer monetization tools are likely to emerge. We lower our TP to \$800 to account for elevated CapEx spend and lower/negative FCF, and we reiterate our Buy rating. What We Liked: 1) Meta's Product Roadmap Coming into Focus…with CEO Zuckerberg suggesting AI is accelerating its product development cycle and we note product announcements around Meta’s Personal and Business Agents, the Muse family of FM models (Spark 1.1, Image, Video) and APIs, Meta AI (+60% more users post integrating Spark), Meta glasses, new apps (with Threads now at 500M MAUs, Forum and Seller), and Meta One, its subscription offerings (Figures 2-3) that we believe can lead to greater visibility and newer revenue streams; 2) Ranking & Recommendation benefits from LLMs Integrations—with LLMs driving +15bps more sessions on IG as R&R improvements drove a +DD Y/Y lift in global time spent on IG and +9% FB video time spent (10%+ in US & Canada) with engagement gains benefiting from content targeting improvements based friends/people a user follows, new to you creators, and Meta’s Muse Image and Video models this as IG passed 2B DAUs in 2Q; – 3) Meta Generative Recommender Ad Model Improving Conversions—that leverages LLM reasoning around ad content and user preferences that has resulted in +1% higher IG app event conversions in pilots and when (Continued…)

– 4) Advantage+ ARR reaches \$75B+ as GenAI Creative Adopted by 9M+ Businesses (+1M Q/Q)—\$75B+ ARR compares to \$60B+ in 3Q25 with image generation adoption 2x+ Q/Q (including from video assets), as Meta rolls out new E2E creative solutions and Agency integrations; and
– 5) Business Agent Opportunity Emerging—1M+ businesses are using Business Agents weekly on WA & Messenger and the product expanding to Instagram, and monetized via subscriptions (Meta One) and pricing based on volumes (tokens) and message delivery.
What We’re Watching:
1) CapEx Investments as Meta’s Product Pipeline Ramps…as Meta raises the low-end of its ’26 capex guide by \$5B to \$130-\$145B and is focused on maximizing capacity in ‘26 and ‘27 (potentially reaching 14GW by ’27) amidst continued industry supply-constraints with management suggesting most of its compute would be allocated to its core business, personal agents, and new products and we now project CapEx to reach \$205B and \$249B in ’27E and ‘28E;
– 2) …With Enterprise a Potential New Monetization Stream with Meta Compute—that can include Compute, Intelligence, Agentic, and Coding offerings (among others) as Meta’s model API launches to more distribution channels shortly, though we’re watching Meta’s capacity given our view that Meta remains capacity constrained and is prioritizing its core O&O products, while noting significant demand for its compute capacity and we believe it has converted some of its sales force to Enterprise;
– 3) Legal & Regulatory Headwinds—we highlight the \$2.4B in legal charges in 2Q and Meta flagged multiple youth-related trials scheduled in the US for the remainder of 2026 that could result in additional losses; and
4) Potential for Negative FCF in 3Q and in ’27E and ‘28E—with 2Q FCF at \$784M, we project FCF to turn negative in 2H26 and to remain negative through ‘28E, highlighting Meta’s trade-off in NT investment to support LT AI capacity and we wouldn’t be surprised to see Meta issue new debt and/or potential equity.
Quarterly Results Recap
Overall Results—Revenue & OI Above Expectations (ex-Legal & Severance Charges): Revenue of \$60.8 billion (+28.0% Y/Y, +26.5% Y/Y ex-FX) came in \~1% above consensus. Operating income of \$18.8 billion (30.9% margin) came in \~12% below consensus and GAAP EPS of \$6.18 compares to consensus of \$7.20. But adjusting for Meta’s \$2.4 billion legal charge in G&A and \$1.18 billion in severance expenses, 2Q OI would have come in \~9% above our projections.
Family of Apps: Revenue & Profitability Above (ex-Legal & Severance): Family of Apps DAPs of 3.60 billion (+3% Y/Y, +1.1% Q/Q) came in \~1% below our projection, revenue of \$60.4 billion (+28.0% Y/Y) was in-line with our projection, led by US & Canada acceleration in advertising revenue growth of +31.4% Y/Y (ad pricing +20% Y/Y) aiding 26.0% Y/Y advertising ex-FX growth, while Family of Apps OI of \$23.4 billion (38.8% margin) compares to our \$25.6 billion projection (42.5% margin).

Reality Labs: Operating Losses Better than Expected: Reality Labs revenue of \$431 million (+16.5% Y/Y) came in above our \$414 million projection while RL Operating Losses of \~\$(4.6) billion compares to our \$(5.1) billion projection. Guidance: 3Q Revenue Guide Below Expectations: Meta’s 3Q revenue guidance range of \$61-\$64B (+19.0%-24.9% Y/Y, +20.0%-25.9% Y/Y ex-FX) was \~1% below consensus at the midpoint on continued R&R model benefits and assumes a \~1pt FX headwind. Meta’s +23.0% Y/Y ex-FX revenue growth guidance at the midpoint includes the following three headwinds: 1) Lapping stronger impressions growth in 3Q25 (R&R improvements on IG Feed & Reels and ad load optimization on IG Feed & Stories) and we believe 4Q25; 2) Impacts from less personalized ad offerings in the EU (now fully rolled out); and 3) Continued integrity enforcement efforts. 2026 CapEx & Expense Guides Narrowed: Meta narrowed 2026 CapEx guidance to a range of \$130B-\$145B (from \$125B-\$145B), \~2% below our projection at the midpoint, while narrowing 2026 Expense guide to \$165B-\$169B (from \$162B-\$169B), +42% Y/Y at the midpoint and \~2% above our projections at the midpoint. Bigger picture, we believe this updated guidance reflects Meta’s \~10% RIF with spend reallocated towards Meta Compute.

Meta Platforms Inc
Company description
Meta Platforms, Inc. is a multinational social media and networking application development company. Through various tools, Meta allows users to connect, share, discover, and communicate with one another over computers and mobile devices. Meta also provides developers with tools to build websites and applications.
Investment strategy
We rate Meta Platforms Buy. We view that Reels can effectively compete with other short-form video platforms and that monetization is improving, which we think should continue to see benefits.
Valuation
Our target price of \$800 is based on \~22x our 2027E GAAP EPS of \$36.93 and implies \~11x our 2027E EV/EBITDA. We justify our valuation methodology based on Meta’s user scale, growing engagement, product super cycle and AI opportunity, ads innovation, and revenue growth, and we’re watching investments and overall profitability.
Risks
Risks to our target price include: 1) Impacts from changes to ATT and IDFA could prove more difficult to overcome and structurally impact Meta’s advertising business; 2) Online advertising spend could decelerate faster than we anticipate; 3) Competition could prove to be more impactful than we anticipate; 4) Meta may not be able to achieve meaningful contributions from its investments in non-advertising businesses (metaverse). 5) Adverse economic and/or consumer spending trends could hinder advertising spend; and 6) Regulatory pressures on anti-trust, data, and privacy practices could adversely impact on performance.

Guide to Citi Research Fundamental Research Investment Ratings: Citi Research stock recommendations include an investment rating and an optional risk rating to highlight high risk stocks. Risk rating takes into account both price volatility and fundamental criteria. Stocks will either have no risk rating or a High risk rating assigned. Investment Ratings: Citi Research investment ratings are Buy, Neutral and Sell. Our ratings are a function of analyst expectations of expected total return ("ETR") and risk. ETR is the sum of the forecast price appreciation (or depreciation) plus the dividend yield for a stock within the next 12 months. The target price is based on a 12 month time horizon. The Investment rating definitions are: Buy (1) ETR of 15% or more or 25% or more for High risk stocks; and Sell (3) for negative ETR. Any covered stock not assigned a Buy or a Sell is a Neutral (2). For stocks rated Neutral (2), if an analyst believes that there are insufficient valuation drivers and/or investment catalysts to derive a positive or negative investment view, they may elect with the approval of Citi Research management not to assign a target price and, thus, not derive an ETR. Citi Research may suspend its rating and target price and assign “Rating Suspended” status for regulatory and/or internal policy reasons. Citi Research may also suspend its rating and target price and assign "Under Review" status for other exceptional circumstances (e.g. lack of information critical to the analyst's thesis, trading suspension) affecting the company and/or trading in the company's securities. In both such situations, the rating and target price will show as “—“ and “-“ respectively in the rating history price chart. Prior to 11 April 2022 Citi Research assigned “Under Review” status to both situations and prior to 11 Nov 2020 only in exceptional circumstances.
